senses.gloss: f. (קָרַב) coming near, use of the root קָרַב.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 96:4">Gen. R. s. 96</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 47:29">Gen. XLVII, 29</cite>) <he>כל מי שנ׳ בו ק׳ למות וכ׳</he> he of whom the expression ‘come near to die’ is used, has not reached the age of his fathers; <he>דוד כתיב בו ק׳ וכ׳</he> of David the expression <he>קרב</he> is used (<cite ref="I Kings 2:1">I Kings II, 1</cite>) &c.; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 168:5">Yalk. Kings 168</cite>.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 3b:16">Snh. 3ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 22:7">Ex. XXII, 7</cite> <he>ונקרב</he>) <he>משעת ק׳ שלשה</he> from the time of the approach (before court) there must be three judges.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 71:5">Gen. R. s. 71</cite> <he>בזה ק׳ ובזה ק׳</he> coming near is mentioned in connection with the tribe of Judah (<cite ref="Psalms 65:5">Ps. LXV, 5</cite>) and with the priestly tribe (<cite ref="Exodus 28">Ex. XXVIII</cite>, .
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 7:7:4">Y. Snh. VII, 25ᵃ</cite> <he>מכיון דכתיב ק׳ ק׳ וכ׳</he> since with regard to illicit connections the word <he>קרב</he> is used &c.
<cite ref="Shabbat 104b:9">Sabb. 104ᵇ</cite> <he>מחוסר ק׳</he>, <he>מחוסר מעשה דק׳</he> it lacks being brought together (joined into one word); a. fr.—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Horayot 2:5:4">Y. Hor. II, 46ᵈ</cite> <he>ק׳ פרישה</he> the root <he>קרב</he> may also mean separation (coming near one’s self, ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 65:5">Is. LXV, 5</cite>).—Pl. <cite ref="S02036"><he>קְרֵיבוֹת</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Pesachim 118b:17">Pes. 118ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 68:31">Ps. LXVIII, 31</cite>) <he>מי גרם … ק׳ שהיו חפצין בהן</he> what caused the dispersion of Israel among the nations? The approaches (to the nations) which they desired; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 800:1">Yalk. Ps. 800</cite> <cite ref="S01891"><he>קְרֵבוֹת</he></cite> (or <he>קְרָבוֹת</he>).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:1:13">Y. Ber. IX, 13ᵃ</cite> top, v. <cite ref="S01926"><he>קָרוֹב</he> I</cite>.
